summary: Marcel Hofinger worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte.

Marcel Mauss studied at Bordeaux, EPHE, Leiden, Utrecht, and Oxford under Durkheim, Lévi, Meillet, and others. A scholar of religious studies and philosophy, he taught at EPHE (1901–1940) and held the sociology chair at Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Lévi, Bacot, Przyluski, and Pelliot. She taught at EPHE (1938–1963) and edited the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
Marco Ferrante works in Indology and philosophy. He has held posts at the University of Rome (attested 2014) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Marco Walther, a scholar of Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Munich (attested 2017) under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Würzburg, Nagoya, and Heidelberg, he held positions at the Dharma Drum institutions, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a Junior Research Fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and a professorship at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).
Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Seoul National University, Dongguk University, and the University of Prague under doctoral supervisor Radek Chlup.
Marek Zvelebil was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Sheffield (~1974–1976) and later held an academic post there (~1981–2011).
Margaret Cone works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. She was affiliated with the University of Cambridge and Darwin College, Cambridge (attested 1996).
Margaret Dornish specialized in religious studies and Sinology, having studied at USC, CGU, and Yale. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).
Margaret Gouin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed her PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams.

Margaret J. Pearson works in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington under Hellmut Wilhelm and Burton Watson, and was a Visiting Fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge (1997).

Margaret Mead studied at Barnard and Columbia under Franz Boas. Her major career posts included the American Museum of Natural History (1926–1969), Columbia University (1954–1978), Fordham University (1968–1970), and the University of Rhode Island (1970).

Margaret R. Miles, a scholar of religious studies and history, earned her PhD from the Graduate Theological Union. She held posts at Harvard University and Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and served as dean of the Graduate Theological Union (1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under Linda Penkower and pursued postdoctoral studies under Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya was a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at St. Petersburg University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, she worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–2021) and IOM RAS (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Karin Preisendanz and completed her MA under Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Reed College and Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, she held a post as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).
Marian Ury was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from UC Berkeley and was a professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis from 1969 to 1995.
